messages:
Alex (AE): Heads-up — Acero POC is hitting failures when using function-calling + JSON mode. Customer sees schema validation errors and some token 429s. Details below, can we swarm?
Maria (SE): Can you paste the exact error + the JSON schema you're providing to the model?
Alex (AE): Error snippet: "InvalidJSONError: payload did not validate against schema: property 'invoice_id' expected type string but got number" Also from their logs: "RateLimitError: 429 - token stream throttle"
Chris (Eng): @Alex thanks. Two separate things likely: (1) model output doesn't match strict schema types, (2) streaming token throttles can cut JSON objects mid-chunk and break the validator. Please share request_id and sample request.
Alex (AE): request_id: req_01H8Z9K, model: rwd-instruct-1-large (quantized), payload we send below.
Alex (AE): ```json
{"function_name":"create_invoice","arguments_schema":{
  "type":"object",
  "properties":{
    "invoice_id": {"type":"string"},
    "amount": {"type":"number"}
  },
  "required":["invoice_id","amount"]
}
```
Maria (SE): Got it. what does the model actually return (raw)? sometimes it returns unquoted numeric id: {"invoice_id": 12345, "amount": 100.0}. That will fail the validator.
Alex (AE): Yes raw: ```json
{"invoice_id": 12345, "amount": 100.0}
```
Chris (Eng): Two mitigation paths: 
- Quick workaround: change schema to accept string|number for invoice_id ("type":["string","number"]) or coerce in post-processing.
- Better: instruct the model to stringify the id in the function signature / prompt. e.g. prompt suffix: "Return invoice_id as a string (quoted)."
Also: for streaming 429s try disabling streaming (stream: false) or implement incremental-JSON-reassembly on client.
Sophie (Support): I checked their tenant usage — they're on a small trial plan. The 429s look like burst token throttling from shared capacity. Recommend offering a short Dedicated trial or request a quota bump for the demo.
Alex (AE): Good call. We'll try stringify + disable streaming. Any code snippet for disabling streaming in SDK?
Maria (SE): SDK example: ```js
client.responses.create({ model: 'rwd-instruct-1-large', input: prompt, stream: false, function_call: { name: 'create_invoice', mode: 'auto' }, json_schema: schema })
```
Chris (Eng): Also ensure the tool / function output sets Content-Type: application/json in tool metadata so our parser treats output as JSON and doesn't try heuristic extraction. If you must stream, buffer until a full JSON is detected before validation.
Alex (AE): Trying fixes now. Also noticed in our logs a bunch of "split_chunk" warnings at the tokenizer level when streaming long embeddings. Could that correlate?
Chris (Eng): Possibly — if a chunk boundary splits inside a string token the client may see truncated JSON. Tokenizer-level splits matter for streaming. For POC we usually disable stream to avoid that class of errors.
Sophie (Support): I've provisioned a temporary quota bump for their org (org_acero_demo) for 48h and opened a Dedicated trial quote. Notified sales finance.
Alex (AE): Awesome thanks. I'll re-run the POC with schema updated and streaming off. If it still fails I'll paste the full debug dump.
deploy-bot: capacity-autoscaler: scaled sales-poc pool +2 gpus due to burst (autoscale event id: ae-2026-04-12-77) :rocket:
Maria (SE): If they need a durable solution, propose: (A) update schema to accept either type and validate server-side, (B) add a pre-flight prompt instruction to enforce stringification, (C) enable Dedicated to avoid burst throttles.
Chris (Eng): If they hit the validator edge-case again capture the exact model output and request id; send to /internal/debug?req=req_01H8Z9K and include a dump of the full streaming chunks. We can patch the validator to offer a tolerant mode for POCs.
Alex (AE): Will do. Demo scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PT with Acero PM. I'll include these workarounds in the runbook. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Sophie (Support): I'll follow up with the Dedicated trial docs and the quota ticket number.
Alex (AE): Closing loop after demo, will file a short postmortem if anything persists. :heart:
